sources.productionSourceHashDefinition: SHA256 of sorted compact JSON mapping repository-relative non-test Go, SQL, go.mod and go.sum paths to their SHA256
sources.sourceOrigin: Independent exact-tag baseline and isolated optimization candidate; measurements did not use the moving development worktree

environment.storageIsolation: Fresh disposable SQLite directories or unique PostgreSQL schemas in the owned test cluster

methods.comparison: One unprofiled baseline then candidate pair for each provider and workload; no reverse-order repetition or best-result selection
methods.ordinary: Real loopback TCP HTTP; 10000 items, 8 clients, 200 requests each for board/bootstrap/mixed. Board has 4 columns and 120 cards. Mixed has 40 creates and 160 reads. Setup, numbering and warmup are outside timing.
methods.status: 200 HTTP-created todo items, 200 doing PATCH then 200 done PATCH at concurrency 8. Per-phase timing/CPU excludes setup and metric serialization.
methods.sql: Separate direct handler probe using existing settings and user; excludes HTTP authentication and transaction entry. Status probes are rolled back before real HTTP workload. QueryRow INSERT/UPDATE RETURNING is classified as DML from saved SQL text.
methods.schedules: 1000 due rules and 1000 ordinary items, one production generation-helper lane, four ordinary TCP readers maintained until all rules finish. No reader request-count cutoff. Also 100 same-period HTTP calls racing one worker.
methods.events: 25 matching rules times 40 events, HTTP admission concurrency 8 then sequential production event transaction helpers. Four TCP readers cover complete admission and processing. Autonomous coordinator scheduling overhead is not measured.
methods.cpu: Go test CPU and allocation figures include Home plus the local HTTP client; SQLite runs in that process. PostgreSQL server CPU is excluded. No cross-provider total-CPU claim.
methods.idle: Candidate native SQLite Home only; no browser or active API calls during sampling. Configuration happens before the window. 100Hz CPU accounting; I/O and SQL are distinct. Historical v0.2.8 idle is not a newly paired RSS comparison.
methods.diagnostics: Short CPU/allocation profiles were collected separately for SQLite board and status. Profiled latencies are not used as formal A/B results; cumulative allocation profiles include profiler allocations.

limits: Single-pass bounded measurements on a shared host, not an SLA, WAN result, sustainable peak capacity, or long-duration soak test.
SQLite ordinary board P95 rose from 159.331 to 168.887 ms in this sample; lower SQL count/allocation and median latency do not prove an improvement in its tail.
Bootstrap control P95 also drifted upward (SQLite 9.388 to 10.372 ms; PostgreSQL 10.973 to 13.635 ms); this is retained, not used to explain away every change.
SQLite event-window board P95 was 103.443 to 104.804 ms; event completion and CPU improved but front-end tail improvement was not established.
Native idle observations cover only the candidate SQLite Home process, not PostgreSQL background work. Zero measured ticks or I/O does not prove absolute zero cost or independently prove zero SQL.
Worker, coordinator and notification code was unchanged, so executor load, notification-limit scenarios and the historical baseline native idle were not rerun.
Request-pool wait is cumulative across concurrent calls and excludes earlier waiting such as the application write gate.
Required record semantics remain: each state workload has 200 completed cycle observations and no unexpected item revisions.
releaseAssociation: Historical isolated optimization comparison against exact v0.2.8, before short-ID main commit edbd0e0 was integrated. Version 0.3.1 preserves the 0.3.0 short-ID API; final integrated measurements are recorded separately. Original measurement labels and hashes are retained.
